The Maroochy Problem
CS 581 · Nuclear Cybersecurity · Workshop 2

The Maroochy Problem

Eight graduate students were asked to card five threat actors spanning at least three types. Working separately, all eight chose the same insider case. Then they split on what to do once they got there. Contributions are identified by the plant system each student operates, not by name.

40cards
26distinct actors
8/8chose the same insider case
2named the individual
The finding

The rule covered the picture, not the name

The assignment forbade depicting a real person. It said nothing about naming one. The Maroochy Water Services incident is the canonical ICS insider case, so a taxonomy requiring an insider type sends everyone to the same place: a real, convicted, named individual. Every student in the cohort landed there without being pointed at it.

“No card may depict a real person.”

Both groups complied. One group read the rule; the other read past it to the reason behind it. That gap is the thing worth teaching, and no one planned it.
